## Vocabulary

## Definitions

- [statement] A null entry from getSignatureStatuses means the status was not found, not that the transaction failed. The method searches only a recent status cache unless searchTransactionHistory is true. A null can mean dropped, never landed, or evicted from the cache. Treat the transaction as dead only after block height passes lastValidBlockHeight and a history search also returns null. (medium confidence) — https://www.helius.dev/docs/rpc/guides/getsignaturestatuses.md · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://github.com/fardream/confirm-solana-transaction
- [statement] FullSend is a separate, access-gated Jito product: a Solana JSON-RPC sendTransaction endpoint that forwards signed transactions straight to current and upcoming leaders through stake-weighted QoS. It does not simulate transactions or track confirmation. Solana Compass reports that Jito's BAM maintenance notice says validators, FullSend users and standard bundle senders need take no action for the Alpenglow transition. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05) — https://docs.jito.wtf/fullsend/ · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://solanacompass.com/news/jito-details-bams-alpenglow-plan-maintenance-mode-for-all-mainnet-nodes-no-firebam-during-the-transition
- [statement] FullSend is a separate, access-form-gated Jito service: a Solana-compatible JSON-RPC sendTransaction at https://mainnet.hudson.jito.wtf with an api_key query parameter, direct-to-leader SWQOS delivery, validator blacklists for MEV protection (default and custom, both on by default), and a browser-safe sendTransactionWeb that authenticates by authorized fee-payer signer. It runs no simulation and tracks no confirmation. Jito's BAM changelog says FullSend users needed no action during the Alpenglow BAM maintenance window. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05) — https://github.com/jito-labs/jito-docs/blob/main/docs/source/fullsend.md · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://bam.dev/blog/bam-changelog-sept-23-oct-9/
- [statement] A keypair file written by solana-keygen is a JSON array of exactly 64 byte values: the first 32 bytes are the Ed25519 secret seed and the last 32 bytes are the public key. Metaplex states the file 'must be a JSON array of 64 numbers'. (high confidence) — https://kevinheavey.github.io/solders/tutorials/keypairs.html · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://docs.rs/crate/solana-keypair/latest/source/src/lib.rs, https://metaplex.com/docs/solana/solana-keypairs-and-wallets, https://mattmazur.com/2021/11/19/splitting-a-solana-keypair-into-a-public-and-private-keys/
- [statement] A Solana CLI keypair file is a JSON array of exactly 64 byte values: the first 32 are the Ed25519 secret seed and the last 32 are the public key. `solana-keygen new` writes it to ~/.config/solana/id.json unless --outfile is given (Agave builds home_dir/.config/solana/id.json). Metaplex states the file 'must be a JSON array of 64 numbers'. (high confidence) — https://kevinheavey.github.io/solders/tutorials/keypairs.html · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://docs.rs/crate/solana-keypair/latest/source/src/lib.rs, https://metaplex.com/docs/solana/solana-keypairs-and-wallets, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anza-xyz/agave/master/keygen/src/keygen.rs
- [statement] The base fee is a flat 5,000 lamports per required signature. It does not depend on the CUs the transaction requests or uses. The priority fee is charged on top of the base fee. (high confidence) — https://chorus.one/reports-research/transaction-latency-on-solana-do-swqos-priority-fees-and-jito-tips-make-your-transactions-land-faster · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://www.helius.dev/blog/solana-fees-in-theory-and-practice, https://docs.chainstack.com/docs/solana-transaction-v1
- [statement] @solana/kit is the renamed 2.x line of @solana/web3.js. It is functional (no classes except SolanaError), fully tree-shakable, uses Web Crypto Ed25519 so key and signing operations are async, supports native bigint, and has zero third-party dependencies. It is not backward-compatible with web3.js 1.x. (high confidence) — https://github.com/anza-xyz/kit · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://blog.triton.one/intro-to-the-new-solana-kit-formerly-web3-js-2/, https://www.quicknode.com/guides/solana-development/tooling/web3js/migrate-to-v3
- [statement] Kit has no Connection or Transaction classes. Moving a web3.js v1 codebase to Kit means rewriting every call site, and libraries such as Anchor's TypeScript client did not plug into Kit. The @solana/compat package offers conversion helpers between legacy and Kit types. (high confidence) — https://www.quicknode.com/guides/solana-development/tooling/web3js/migrate-to-v3 · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://github.com/anza-xyz/kit
- [statement] A v0 message is a legacy message plus a 0x80 version prefix byte and an address_table_lookups array after the instructions. Each lookup names a table by its 32-byte address and lists one-byte writable and read-only indexes into it. The runtime appends the resolved writable addresses, then the read-only ones, to the static keys, and instructions index into that combined list. A lookup that selects no accounts fails sanitization. (high confidence) — https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/docs/en/core/transactions/versioned-transactions.mdx · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://docs.anza.xyz/proposals/versioned-transactions, https://github.com/anza-xyz/solana-sdk/blob/master/message/src/versions/v0/mod.rs
- [statement] New table entries are not usable in the slot where they were added. The table stores last_extended_slot and last_extended_slot_start_index. While the current slot equals last_extended_slot, a lookup sees only the entries before that start index. A transaction that references a newer entry in the same slot fails. (high confidence) — https://docs.rs/solana-address-lookup-table-interface/3.1.0/src/solana_address_lookup_table_interface/state.rs.html · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://docs.anza.xyz/proposals/versioned-transactions, https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/docs/en/core/transactions/versioned-transactions.mdx, https://github.com/solana-program/address-lookup-table/blob/main/program/src/processor.rs
- [statement] Do not catch -32015 and return null or 'not found'. It means the request failed on a versioned transaction, not that the transaction is missing. Helius says -32015 in logs already shows a project failing on versioned transactions. A payment-detection loop that swallows it reports a landed transaction as lost. (medium confidence) — https://www.helius.dev/docs/rpc/transaction-v1.md · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/docs/en/core/transactions/versioned-transactions.mdx, https://dev.to/timothymycompc/solana-rpc-error-32015-why-4-in-10-transactions-vanish-from-your-app-26cm

## Structure and components

- [statement] A Solana keypair file is plaintext and the generation passphrase does not protect it. Anza's file-system wallet page says 'This file contains your unencrypted keypair', 'File system wallets are the least secure method of storing SOL tokens', and that even with a password 'that password applies to the recovery seed phrase, not the file'. Matt Mazur's walkthrough shows the CLI prompt itself saying the passphrase improves the seed phrase 'NOT the keypair file itself, which is stored as insecure plain text'. Anza's page gives no file-permission advice. (high confidence) — https://docs.anza.xyz/cli/wallets/file-system · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://mattmazur.com/2021/11/19/splitting-a-solana-keypair-into-a-public-and-private-keys/

## How it works

- [statement] A successful sendTransaction response returns only a signature. It does not show that the cluster will process or finalize the transaction. The caller must poll getSignatureStatuses, because the RPC can return a signature for a transaction that is later dropped. (high confidence) — https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/cookbook/transactions/retry.mdx · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://onfinality.io/en/learn/solana-rpc-timeout-and-retries
- [statement] Fetching a blockhash at processed can pick a blockhash from a minority fork that the cluster later abandons. The transaction is then dropped with the blockhash not found. Official docs advise confirmed or finalized when polling getLatestBlockhash. Helius calls confirmed the best practice for sending and states that processed is not recommended for production-critical flows. (high confidence) — https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/cookbook/transactions/retry.mdx · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://www.helius.dev/blog/solana-commitment-levels, https://www.helius.dev/blog/how-to-deal-with-blockhash-errors-on-solana
- [statement] sendTransaction returns only the transaction id (the first signature). A successful response says nothing about whether the cluster will process or finalize the transaction, and the RPC can hand back a signature for a transaction that is later dropped. A bot must poll getSignatureStatuses to learn the outcome. (high confidence) — https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/cookbook/transactions/retry.mdx · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://onfinality.io/en/learn/solana-rpc-timeout-and-retries, https://www.helius.dev/docs/rpc/guides/getsignaturestatuses.md
- [statement] A fee-bumped rebroadcast is a different transaction. Changing the compute-unit price changes the message, so the message hash and signature change and the AlreadyProcessed check does not link the two. RPC Fast describes rebroadcasting 'with a slightly higher priority fee' when a transaction is not processed within 2 slots. By the official guide's logic both versions can land while the blockhash is valid. Guard such intents on-chain (Circuit added a sequence-enforcer instruction with TTL checks) or accept duplicates. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/anza-xyz/agave/blob/v4.4.0/runtime/src/bank/check_transactions.rs · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/cookbook/transactions/retry.mdx, https://rpcfast.com/blog/how-to-land-transactions-solana, https://circuittrading.notion.site/November-10-2024-JLP-Vaults-Post-Mortem-13b1385fd0f58031b7acde64235c4852
- [statement] Two intentionally identical transactions collide. The duplicate check keys on the whole message hash, so the same fee payer, instructions, accounts and blockhash give AlreadyProcessed on the second send. Change the message (a fresh blockhash or different instruction data) to send a distinct second transaction. Chainstack also warns that transactions can be treated as duplicates when many share a blockhash. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/anza-xyz/agave/blob/v4.4.0/runtime/src/bank/check_transactions.rs · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://docs.chainstack.com/docs/solana-how-to-handle-the-transaction-expiry-error
- [statement] Do not re-sign with a new blockhash while the first blockhash can still land. The Solana retry guide calls confirming expiry first 'very important' because both transactions can be accepted. Chainstack and the fardream library say the same. The safe order: rebroadcast identical bytes until block height is past lastValidBlockHeight, make a final status lookup, then rebuild. (high confidence) — https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/cookbook/transactions/retry.mdx · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://docs.chainstack.com/docs/solana-how-to-handle-the-transaction-expiry-error, https://github.com/fardream/confirm-solana-transaction
- [statement] Jito tips and Solana priority fees are separate levers: the tip ranks the bundle in the Block Engine auction, the priority fee affects runtime scheduling. Tips do nothing when the leader is not Jito-Solana. For single transactions via Jito sendTransaction, Jito advises setting both a priority fee and a tip; Chainstack suggests a 70/30 split between them. (medium confidence) — https://docs.jito.wtf/lowlatencytxnsend/ · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://rpcfast.com/blog/how-to-improve-your-jito-bundle-landing-rate-on-solana, https://docs.chainstack.com/docs/solana-mev-protection
- [statement] The Block Engine sendTransaction path (https://mainnet.block-engine.jito.wtf/api/v1/transactions) proxies Solana's sendTransaction to the validator with MEV protection on by default and always sets skip_preflight=true, so the RPC does not simulate the transaction first. The query parameter bundleOnly=true sends the transaction only as a single-transaction bundle, which gives revert protection. When the send was made as a bundle, the bundle ID comes back in the x-bundle-id response header. (medium confidence) — https://docs.jito.wtf/lowlatencytxnsend/ · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://gist.github.com/zhe-t/60938c69e29276b7a9f098e1b0672c79
- [statement] If transactions from your bundle show up on an explorer as individual failed transactions, suspect an uncled block. When a block built by a leader is not accepted by the supermajority, any party that received it can rebroadcast its transactions, and those go through the normal banking stage without bundle atomicity or revert protection. Jito's mitigations are pre- and post-account checks so a rebroadcast is harmless, minimizing leakage, and keeping the tip in the same transaction as the strategy. (high confidence) — https://docs.jito.wtf/lowlatencytxnsend/ · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://rpcfast.com/blog/how-to-improve-your-jito-bundle-landing-rate-on-solana
- [statement] Put the tip instruction in the same transaction as the strategy logic with post-transaction checks; if space is short, add slot and balance assertions to a separate tip transaction (Jito's advice). The defence has an Ethereum precedent: Flashbots told users to add a parent-hash check, require(blockhash(block.number - 1) == expectedParentHash), because transactions from an uncled block become visible and targetable ('uncle bandit'); it cited roughly 1 in 20 Ethereum blocks being uncled at the time and the page is marked outdated. (medium confidence) — https://docs.jito.wtf/lowlatencytxnsend/ · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://hackmd.io/@flashbots/use-cases
- [statement] Wallets and fee-injection code that prepend Compute Budget instructions at index 0 break durable-nonce transactions, because the runtime only recognises a nonce transaction when AdvanceNonceAccount is instruction 0. A Phantom user reported on devnet that the modified transaction 'can never land'; the thread was closed by redirecting to support with no public fix confirmed. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-12) — https://github.com/orgs/phantom/discussions/529 · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots
- [statement] Query the writable accounts the transaction will lock (pool, vault, user token accounts, oracle), not program IDs. Only writable accounts enter the per-account map, and an empty account list returns only the block-wide minimum. Re-estimate for each transaction from a recent sample, because hot-account fees move within seconds, and apply a hard per-transaction cap. Jupiter likewise advises capping the price and validating it before signing, because estimates can spike when recent blocks hold extreme bids. (medium confidence) — https://docs.chainstack.com/docs/solana-estimate-priority-fees-getrecentprioritizationfees · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://github.com/anza-xyz/agave/blob/master/runtime/src/prioritization_fee.rs, https://github.com/anza-xyz/agave/blob/master/runtime/src/prioritization_fee_cache.rs, https://orbitflare.com/blog/developers/solana-priority-fee-estimation, https://developers.jup.ag/docs/swap/advanced/compute-units
- [statement] Simulation errors leave no on-chain record. Metaplex tells developers to send with `skipPreflight: true` when they need a failing transaction recorded on chain, with its logs visible in an explorer. The failed transaction still pays its fee, so use this for debugging, not as a default. (medium confidence) — https://metaplex.com/docs/guides/general/how-to-diagnose-solana-transaction-errors · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://github.com/solana-foundation/developer-content/blob/97a223daedfb5c3b696b709e1a9246a861f2141b/docs/core/fees.md
- [statement] Guidance after the compromise: upgrade to 1.95.8 (even when pinned to latest) or downgrade to a version before 1.95.6, and rotate any suspect authority keys, including multisigs, program authorities and server keypairs. Cyfrin added: check yarn.lock or package-lock.json for the bad versions, and keep strict version control and lockfiles. (high confidence) — https://anza.xyz/blog/web3-js-exploit-root-cause-analysis · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jcxm-7wvp-g6p5, https://www.csoonline.com/article/3617893/solana-sdk-backdoored-for-stealing-secrets-private-keys.html, https://www.cyfrin.io/blog/critical-security-alert-solana-web3-js-library-compromise
- [statement] Anza's root-cause analysis says the phished publisher entered a username and password and completed two-factor authentication on an attacker-run clone of the npm site, so two-factor authentication did not stop the attack. (medium confidence) — https://anza.xyz/blog/web3-js-exploit-root-cause-analysis · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://helpnetsecurity.com/2024/12/04/solana-web3-js-supply-chain-compromise
- [statement] In Python, solders (Rust-backed bindings by Kevin Heavey) supplies the core types: Keypair, Pubkey, Instruction, MessageV0, VersionedTransaction, signing and serialization, RPC request and response types, and an in-process LiteSVM. solders does not fetch blockhashes or send transactions; solana-py's AsyncClient does (get_latest_blockhash, send_transaction). solana-py builds on solders types, and its README says anything missing from it 'is probably in solders now'. Solana's docs name both packages and recommend solana-py for networking and async APIs. The solders tutorial recommends versioned transactions 'if you have a choice'. The two install separately (pip install solders; pip install solana). (high confidence) — https://kevinheavey.github.io/solders/tutorials/transactions.html · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://github.com/michaelhly/solana-py, https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/docs/en/clients/community/python.mdx
- [statement] A lookup table holds at most 256 addresses (LOOKUP_TABLE_MAX_ADDRESSES = 256) because entries are addressed by a u8 index. A v0 message references a table by its address plus lists of one-byte indexes for writable and read-only accounts. (high confidence) — https://docs.anza.xyz/proposals/versioned-transactions · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://docs.rs/solana-address-lookup-table-interface/3.1.0/src/solana_address_lookup_table_interface/state.rs.html
- [statement] A lookup table is an on-chain account that holds at most 256 addresses (LOOKUP_TABLE_MAX_ADDRESSES = 256), because entries are addressed by a u8 index. A v0 message names each table by its address and lists one-byte indexes for the writable and the read-only accounts it loads from that table. ExtendLookupTable fails on a full table, on an extend that would pass 256 entries, and on a deactivated table. (high confidence) — https://docs.anza.xyz/proposals/versioned-transactions · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://docs.rs/solana-address-lookup-table-interface/3.1.0/src/solana_address_lookup_table_interface/state.rs.html, https://github.com/solana-program/address-lookup-table/blob/main/program/src/processor.rs
- [statement] Lookup tables supply only non-signer accounts. The fee payer and every signer stay in the static key list. Program IDs invoked by top-level instructions must also be static keys, because the v0 sanitizer rejects program ids loaded from lookup tables so programs can be analysed without chain state. (high confidence) — https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/docs/en/core/transactions/versioned-transactions.mdx · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://docs.anza.xyz/proposals/versioned-transactions, https://github.com/anza-xyz/solana-sdk/blob/master/message/src/versions/v0/mod.rs
- [statement] Do not leave throwaway tables open. Tables never expire, and rent stays locked until the authority deactivates the table and later closes it. A bot that creates a table per route leaks rent unless it tracks and closes them. Rent must cover the table when it is created and after each extension. The Solana Foundation saw thousands to tens of thousands of tables created, extended or closed per day, so this churn is normal on mainnet. (medium confidence) — https://docs.anza.xyz/proposals/versioned-transactions · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://github.com/solana-program/address-lookup-table/blob/main/program/src/processor.rs, https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/media/content/posts/transaction-v1-and-the-alt-trade-off.mdx
- [statement] Routers choose the version, not the bot. Jupiter /build: transactionVersion=1 forces v1 (default '0'). Jupiter /order: maxSupportedTransactionVersion=1 is only a ceiling, so v1 comes back only when Metis wins the route and the order is not gasless. Gasless and auto-sponsored orders are always v0, and the wrong parameter name is silently ignored. DFlow keeps v0 as the default and needs transactionVersion=v1 on /order and /swap. Branch on the version the response reports, and request v1 only for wallets that support it. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://developers.jup.ag/docs/swap/advanced/transaction-versions · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://pond.dflow.net/spot/trading/v1-migration-guide

## How-to and procedures

- [statement] Use your own transaction signatures against your own RPC as the ground truth for 'landed'. Bundle-ID endpoints have short retention (five minutes in flight, recent slots for statuses) and DBI bundles are outside them; keep bundle-status polling for diagnosis only (in-flight state, drop reason). The jito-bundle crate likewise polls both the Jito API and Solana RPC. (medium confidence) — https://bam.dev/docs/bam/dbi/ · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://docs.jito.wtf/lowlatencytxnsend/, https://docs.rs/crate/jito-bundle/0.1.4/source/FOR_USER.md

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] Commitment guidance changed with Alpenglow. The Solana docs say to point new code at finalized, because it now arrives in about 150 ms, and to re-check every timeout, retry or UX delay tuned to 12.8-second finality. They say confirmed will be removed in a later release. Triton One warns not to move to finalized before the node runs Alpenglow, or requests wait the old 12.8 s. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/media/content/upgrades/alpenglow.mdx · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://blog.triton.one/alpenglow-and-your-triton-stack-what-to-update-before-mainnet/
- [statement] Maker Priority (MPP) and Preconfirmations are not general landing routes. MPP: enrolled market makers send pre-signed price updates to a separate UDP endpoint (PTPU) on each BAM Node; they are scheduled first in every auction batch, need no tip, but must pay at least 1 lamport per compute unit; Jito manages enrollment. Preconfirmations: a read-only stream of transactions a BAM leader has committed to executing, sold through Helius and Triton, with a p50 advantage of 5-10 ms over shred feeds in early tests; they are not finality and exist only for BAM leaders. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05) — https://github.com/jito-labs/jito-docs/blob/main/docs/source/mpp.md · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://github.com/jito-labs/jito-docs/blob/main/docs/source/preconfirmations.md, https://solanacompass.com/news/jito-bam-preconfirmations-go-live-on-solana-covering-34-of-network-stake, https://bam.dev/blog/bam-changelog-sept-23-oct-9/
- [statement] Triton extends getRecentPrioritizationFees with an optional percentile parameter, an integer from 1 to 10,000 (5000 is the median, steps of 0.01%). For each block it returns that percentile of the CU prices paid by non-vote transactions; with account addresses it takes the percentile over the transactions that write-lock each account and returns the highest. Without the parameter it returns the standard minimum. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.triton.one/solana/sending-transactions/priority-fees-api.md · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Resending identical signed bytes is harmless because the network executes at most one copy of a given signature. The duplicate risk comes only from building a second, different transaction. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/fardream/confirm-solana-transaction · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/cookbook/transactions/retry.mdx
- [statement] Once a blockhash has expired, resending the same signed bytes cannot succeed: the handler must fetch a fresh blockhash, re-sign and resend, and a generic HTTP retry wrapper does not do that. Retries consume blockhashes and can cost fees, and no retry strategy rescues a badly degraded network, so fail fast and alert. (medium confidence) — https://onfinality.io/en/learn/solana-rpc-timeout-and-retries · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/cookbook/transactions/retry.mdx, https://docs.chainstack.com/docs/solana-how-to-handle-the-transaction-expiry-error
- [statement] One web3.js user reported confirmTransaction throwing the block-height-exceeded error for a transaction that had already finalized, after sending with a confirmed blockhash and confirming at confirmed. The issue tracker bot closed it by pointing to the Agave repo, and no cause was recorded. Treat an expiry exception as a prompt to check the signature status before rebuilding. (low confidence) — https://github.com/solana-labs/solana/issues/35556 · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots
- [statement] Rebroadcasting identical signed bytes cannot execute twice. Agave's check_transactions rejects a message hash that is already in the StatusCache with AlreadyProcessed ('This transaction has already been processed'). The cost is an error, not a double spend. With preflight on, sendTransaction runs a simulation and returns any simulation error, so a Drift keeper-bot log shows 'Transaction simulation failed: This transaction has already been processed'. A rebroadcast loop must treat that error as 'look up the signature', not as failure. Re-sending with skipPreflight true, as the Solana guide's example does, avoids the error. (high confidence) — https://github.com/anza-xyz/agave/blob/6cd331bf6fd0e92c59e847a3aefaac16ff7b7eda/runtime/src/bank/check_transactions.rs · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://github.com/anza-xyz/agave/blob/6cd331bf6fd0e92c59e847a3aefaac16ff7b7eda/rpc/src/rpc.rs, https://github.com/drift-labs/keeper-bots-v2/issues/130, https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/cookbook/transactions/retry.mdx
- [statement] A Jito bundle is a list of up to 5 fully signed transactions that execute sequentially, within a single slot, and atomically: if any transaction fails, none are committed. Bundles cannot cross slot boundaries. (high confidence) — https://docs.jito.wtf/lowlatencytxnsend/ · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://www.quicknode.com/builders-guide/tools/jito-bundles-by-jito-labs, https://cnitarot.github.io/papers/imc26_solana.pdf
- [statement] Transactions are submitted to the Block Engine (JSON-RPC POST /api/v1/bundles, method sendBundle, or gRPC) as base64 strings (recommended); base58 is slow and marked DEPRECATED in Jito's docs. Maximum 5 transactions per request. (high confidence) — https://docs.jito.wtf/lowlatencytxnsend/ · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://www.helius.dev/docs/sending-transactions/send-bundle
- [statement] Jito's default send rate limit is 1 request per second per IP per region, with no auth key needed for default sends; exceeding it returns a 429 or rate-limit error; higher limits need a ticket. Spreading sends across regional Block Engine endpoints (mainnet global plus Amsterdam, Dublin, Frankfurt and others) therefore multiplies capacity. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05) — https://docs.jito.wtf/lowlatencytxnsend/ · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots
- [statement] A Jito bundle is a list of up to 5 fully signed transactions that the Block Engine passes to a Jito-Solana leader to execute sequentially and atomically within one slot. A bundle cannot cross a slot boundary, and if any transaction fails none of the transactions are committed. (high confidence) — https://docs.jito.wtf/lowlatencytxnsend/ · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://cnitarot.github.io/papers/imc26_solana.pdf, https://www.helius.dev/docs/sending-transactions/send-bundle
- [statement] The Block Engine runs parallel auctions. Bundles whose account-lock patterns intersect on a writable account ((w,w), (r,w) or (w,r)) compete in one auction; bundles that do not intersect, or that overlap only on reads, run in separate auctions. Within an auction bundles are ranked by requested tip per requested compute unit, and Jito submits the highest-paying combination to the validator up to a compute-unit limit. (high confidence) — https://docs.jito.wtf/lowlatencytxnsend/ · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://rpcfast.com/blog/jito-explained-bundles-tips-mev-solana
- [statement] Jito's JSON-RPC defaults to base58 transaction encoding, but base58 is deprecated and slow. Send base64 and set the encoding option to base64 explicitly on every sendBundle and sendTransaction call. (high confidence) — https://docs.jito.wtf/lowlatencytxnsend/ · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://www.helius.dev/docs/sending-transactions/send-bundle, https://solana.com/docs/defi/mev-protection
- [statement] When a Block Engine rate limit is exceeded the response is HTTP 429 or a rate-limit error that names the limit hit, and Jito says default sends no longer need an approved auth key. The jito-bundle Rust crate treats 429s, timeouts and on-chain failures as separate cases in its status handling. (medium confidence) — https://docs.jito.wtf/lowlatencytxnsend/ · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://docs.rs/crate/jito-bundle/0.1.4/source/FOR_USER.md
- [statement] Jito's documented default limit is 1 request per second per IP per region; a higher limit needs a support ticket. This number comes from one source, Jito's docs, and no second source confirms it. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05) — https://docs.jito.wtf/lowlatencytxnsend/ · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots
- [statement] Wrapping a sandwich-prone transaction in your own bundle keeps an attacker from including it in a sandwich bundle, because bundles cannot be nested on Jito. Jupiter's MEV-protection setting works this way by issuing a length-one bundle. The IMC authors caution that this does not stop all front-running, and Solana's guide adds that tight slippage is the most effective single defense. (medium confidence) — https://cnitarot.github.io/papers/imc26_solana.pdf · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://discuss.jup.ag/t/transaction-broadcasting-on-jup-ag/23069, https://solana.com/docs/defi/mev-protection
- [statement] Never put a Jito tip account in an address lookup table. Jito warns that tips must not use lookup tables, the jito-bundle crate validates this up front because a lookup table that contains a tip account makes the transaction fail at runtime, and Solana's dontfront guide repeats the rule (the dontfront account itself may be loaded through a table). (high confidence) — https://docs.jito.wtf/lowlatencytxnsend/ · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://docs.rs/crate/jito-bundle/0.1.4/source/FOR_USER.md, https://solana.com/docs/defi/mev-protection
- [statement] Alternatives to Jito submission trade away atomicity or coverage. Gerus Lab (a vendor blog) says QuickNode's Lil-JIT cannot guarantee atomic multi-transaction execution, and that Astralane's private relay has smaller validator coverage than Jito and an extra relay hop. RPC Fast says some of Jito's tip share moved to Astralane and Lil-JIT in Q1 2026. Neither source publishes measurements. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-07) — https://dev.to/gerus_team/mev-protection-on-solana-in-2026-jito-bundles-astralane-and-what-actually-works-3gbc · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://rpcfast.com/blog/jito-explained-bundles-tips-mev-solana
- [statement] A Jito bundle is up to five fully signed transactions that run in the listed order, atomically and all-or-nothing, inside one slot (a bundle cannot cross a slot boundary). Only a leader running Jito-Solana or BAM can process it; Jito's docs say tips do nothing on leaders that are not Jito-Solana. (high confidence) — https://docs.jito.wtf/lowlatencytxnsend/ · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://github.com/jito-labs/jito-docs/blob/main/docs/source/bundles.md, https://bam.dev/docs/bam/dbi/
- [statement] Block Engine sendBundle (JSON-RPC POST /api/v1/bundles) takes up to five fully signed transactions and returns a bundle_id, the SHA-256 hash of the transaction signatures, on acceptance only. The encoding option defaults to base58 (slow, deprecated), so pass {'encoding': 'base64'} explicitly when sending base64 strings. sendTransaction on /api/v1/transactions proxies to the validator, always sets skip_preflight=true, and with ?bundleOnly=true goes out only as a one-transaction bundle for revert protection; the bundle ID then arrives in the x-bundle-id response header. (high confidence) — https://docs.jito.wtf/lowlatencytxnsend/ · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://www.helius.dev/docs/sending-transactions/send-bundle, https://www.quicknode.com/docs/solana/sendTransaction-jito
- [statement] DBI error and limit behaviour: HTTP 401 means no valid UUID in x-jito-auth; HTTP 429 means the per-key limit was exceeded (applied separately at each BAM node; QUIC drops excess packets instead; the numeric limit is set when the key is issued and not published); QUIC application close code 2 means the keypair is not allowlisted or not yet active, or connections from one IP arrive too fast, so reconnect with backoff, not in a tight loop. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-04) — https://bam.dev/docs/bam/dbi/ · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots
- [statement] Metaplex advises separate keypairs per purpose ('Never use the same keypair for mainnet testing and production') so test scripts cannot send real SOL. (low confidence) — https://metaplex.com/docs/solana/solana-keypairs-and-wallets · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots
- [statement] The Rust Signer trait separates infallible and fallible calls, and the infallible ones hide failure. pubkey() and sign_message() default to try_pubkey() / try_sign_message() with unwrap_or_default(), returning the all-zeros Pubkey or Signature when the signer cannot act. A local Keypair never fails (its try_sign_message always returns Ok and is_interactive is false), but remote or hardware signers report SignerError variants such as Connection, NoDeviceFound and UserCancel, so bot code that signs through a remote signer should call the try_* methods and check is_interactive. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.rs/crate/solana-signer/latest/source/src/lib.rs · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://docs.rs/crate/solana-keypair/latest/source/src/lib.rs
- [statement] Limit the blast radius of a file wallet. Metaplex's matrix pairs local testing with a no-passphrase file wallet, devnet/testnet with a file wallet and backed-up seed, small mainnet amounts with a passphrase-protected file wallet on an encrypted disk, and significant value with a hardware wallet or multisig; it also says never to reuse a keypair across mainnet testing and production. Anza likewise says large balances should not sit in a file system wallet. For a bot, that points to a dedicated hot key funded only with working capital (inference). (medium confidence) — https://metaplex.com/docs/solana/solana-keypairs-and-wallets · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://docs.anza.xyz/cli/wallets/file-system
- [statement] Standard method for sizing the limit: simulate the transaction with a high placeholder limit, read unitsConsumed, then set SetComputeUnitLimit to that value plus a 10-20% margin. The margin covers state changes between simulation and execution; the simulated figure can be higher or lower than what the landed transaction uses. (high confidence) — https://docs.chainstack.com/docs/solana-compute-budget · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://orbitflare.com/blog/developers/solana-priority-fee-estimation, https://github.com/solana-labs/solana-web3.js/pull/2703
- [statement] Code that reads limits or fees by scanning Compute Budget instructions finds nothing on v1 transactions. Read transactionConfig first and fall back to the instruction scan for legacy and v0. To compare a v0 rate with a v1 total, convert the rate with ceil(price * CU limit / 1,000,000). JSON-RPC readers need maxSupportedTransactionVersion set to the integer 1, or getBlock and getTransaction fail with error -32015 on v1 data. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-15) — https://docs.chainstack.com/docs/solana-transaction-v1 · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://solanacompass.com/news/transaction-v1-simd-0385-is-live-on-solana-mainnet-at-epoch-1035, https://www.quicknode.com/guides/solana-development/transactions/how-to-optimize-solana-transactions
- [statement] Agave's scheduler ranks queued transactions by priority = reward x 1,000,000 / (1 + cost). Reward is the validator's fee income: the priority fee plus the non-burned share of the base fee. Cost is the cost-model total for signatures, write locks, instruction data, program execution (the requested or default CU limit) and loaded-accounts data. Rank therefore depends on lamports per unit of total requested cost, not on the micro-lamport price alone. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://github.com/anza-xyz/agave/blob/master/core/src/transaction_priority.rs · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/docs/en/core/fees/fee-structure.mdx
- [statement] Because requested CUs sit in the cost denominator, a tighter CU limit (and a tighter loaded-accounts data limit) raises a transaction's rank at the same total lamport fee, while raising only the price spends more for the same cost. A practitioner post argues that right-sizing the CU limit moves rank more than a higher price does. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/anza-xyz/agave/blob/master/core/src/transaction_priority.rs · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/docs/en/core/fees/fee-structure.mdx, https://dev.to/sulimanmukhtar/solana-priority-fee-estimation-the-rpc-returns-a-minimum-2gba
- [statement] Averages, medians or percentiles of the raw per-slot values are statistics of floors, not of what landed transactions paid. In congestion the distribution above the floor widens where this call cannot see it, so such estimates run low exactly when it matters. The reverse also happens: one overpaying transaction on a quiet account sets that account's value for the whole slot. Triton calls the default value often zero and a poor signal for the competitive fee. (medium confidence) — https://dev.to/sulimanmukhtar/solana-priority-fee-estimation-the-rpc-returns-a-minimum-2gba · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://docs.chainstack.com/docs/solana-estimate-priority-fees-getrecentprioritizationfees, https://docs.triton.one/solana/sending-transactions/priority-fees-api.md
- [statement] If the limit is below the CUs the transaction needs, execution stops with InstructionError::ComputationalBudgetExceeded ('Computational budget exceeded') and the fee is still charged. Simulation can understate later usage because state moves between simulation and landing (routes, tick arrays, Token-2022 transfer hooks). A variable-cost swap therefore needs a larger margin than a fixed-cost transfer, and a re-simulation close to submission. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/anza-xyz/solana-sdk/blob/master/instruction-error/src/lib.rs · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/docs/en/core/fees/fee-structure.mdx, https://developers.jup.ag/docs/swap/advanced/compute-units, https://dev.to/verixia_233e4721792ce3390/optimizing-solana-compute-unit-limits-for-swap-execution-3di4
- [statement] A simulation reflects one RPC node's view. If the node lags, a dependent simulation can fail with missing-account errors because it has not seen a just-confirmed transaction. The program-metadata CU estimator hit this on a hosted devnet RPC, and the suggested fix is to pass the confirmation slot as minContextSlot to simulateTransaction and to retry such simulations. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-08-11) — https://github.com/solana-program/program-metadata/issues/105 · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://www.helius.dev/blog/how-to-deal-with-blockhash-errors-on-solana
- [statement] Agave's simulate path builds its batch with prepare_unlocked_batch_from_single_tx ('without locking accounts') and never commits the result. A passing simulation therefore says nothing about write-lock contention with other transactions or about scheduler and block-limit behavior. That consequence is an inference from the code; no doc states it. (low confidence) — https://github.com/anza-xyz/agave/blob/v3.1.8/runtime/src/bank.rs · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots
- [statement] A transaction that fails on chain still costs the fee. Solana's fee docs say the total fee (5,000 lamports per signature plus the priority fee) is deducted before execution and is charged whether the transaction succeeds or fails. A failure caught by preflight costs nothing, because the node rejects it before forwarding. With skipPreflight true, every deterministic error that preflight would have caught is paid for if the transaction lands. The retry guide titles this 'The Cost of Skipping Preflight'. (high confidence) — https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/fa76516c1bac9a70e177a401c82179257c0bf78c/apps/docs/content/docs/en/core/fees/fee-structure.mdx · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/b40ff7bab35dbda5404eb2e22f2d07485f8cbf3f/apps/docs/content/cookbook/transactions/retry.mdx, https://github.com/anza-xyz/agave/blob/v3.1.8/rpc/src/rpc.rs
- [statement] Aggregators can run the simulation for you. Jupiter's v6 /swap parameter dynamicComputeUnitLimit does a swap simulation to set the compute-unit limit and, per its own spec, 'will increase latency slightly since there will be one extra RPC call to simulate this'. QuickNode's Jupiter guide says the API returns a simulated transaction, so skipPreflight can be set true. Jupiter's current docs page says the Metis Swap API is superseded by Swap V2, so these parameter docs may be stale. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://github.com/jup-ag/jupiter-quote-api-node/blob/b6d355c8fb1cfe39d59ed8ad9d9a79697e1af021/swagger.yaml · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://quicknode.com/docs/solana/jupiter-transactions, https://developers.jup.ag/docs/swap-api
- [statement] Addresses appended to a table are not usable in the slot they were added. The proposal says newly appended addresses need one slot to warm up, the program source says a table can only be used to look up addresses extended before the current bank's slot, and tutorials say to wait for the next slot after extend. A bot that extends and then immediately sends or simulates a transaction using the new entries will fail. (high confidence) — https://docs.anza.xyz/proposals/versioned-transactions · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://docs.rs/solana-address-lookup-table-interface/3.1.0/src/solana_address_lookup_table_interface/state.rs.html, https://docs.chainstack.com/docs/solana-address-lookup-tables.md
- [statement] A deactivated table can still be used by transactions until its deactivation slot is no longer present in the SlotHashes sysvar. The table cannot be closed until then. The cool-down exists so in-flight transactions can land and to remove nondeterminism from loading addresses in the slot a table is closed. (high confidence) — https://docs.anza.xyz/proposals/versioned-transactions · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://docs.rs/solana-address-lookup-table-interface/3.1.0/src/solana_address_lookup_table_interface/state.rs.html
- [statement] The program source says it returns a generic error, not a specific one, for deactivated lookup tables, because a specific error would race with the table being closed at any point. A bot caching table accounts can therefore see a generic not-found style failure for a table that was deactivated, not a self-explanatory one. (low confidence) — https://docs.rs/solana-address-lookup-table-interface/3.1.0/src/solana_address_lookup_table_interface/state.rs.html · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots
- [statement] V1 keeps the per-transaction caps at 12 signatures, 64 instructions and 64 account addresses (255 account indexes per instruction); only the byte limit grows. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-15) — https://www.helius.dev/blog/agave-v4-2 · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots
- [statement] Limits the Anza proposal lists for v0 lookups: signers cannot be loaded through a table (full signer addresses stay in the message); hardware wallets cannot show details of accounts referenced through a table; only single-level lookups work; and a transaction may not load the same account twice, whether through account_keys or through a table. (low confidence) — https://docs.anza.xyz/proposals/versioned-transactions · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots
- [statement] Do not catch -32015 and report 'transaction not found'. Helius says that seeing -32015 in logs means the project is already failing on versioned transactions. One developer reports that batch reads (getParsedTransactions, getTransactions) throw for the whole batch when one entry is v1, hiding the other 49 transactions, and that apps returning null on the error mark paid transactions as missing. Older guides hard-code the old setting: OnFinality's lookup-table guide (undated) uses maxSupportedTransactionVersion 0 only, which now fails on v1 data. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-03) — https://www.helius.dev/docs/rpc/transaction-v1.md · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://dev.to/timothymycompc/solana-rpc-error-32015-why-4-in-10-transactions-vanish-from-your-app-26cm, https://onfinality.io/en/learn/solana-versioned-transactions-getblock-rpc
- [statement] FreezeLookupTable makes a table permanently immutable: it can never be extended or closed again, and its authority becomes none. Empty tables and deactivated tables cannot be frozen. A bot that depends on a third-party table can read the authority field. A frozen table can no longer gain entries or be closed out from under the bot. (high confidence) — https://github.com/solana-program/address-lookup-table/blob/main/program/src/processor.rs · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://github.com/solana-program/address-lookup-table/blob/main/program/src/instruction.rs
- [statement] To move an ALT-based builder to v1, resolve each table entry, put the addresses inline in the single address array, and deduplicate them, because v1 rejects duplicates. Stay within 64 addresses and 4,096 bytes. Send transactions over 1,232 raw bytes as base64, since base58 stays capped at 1,232. v1 also defaults the compute-unit limit and loaded-accounts-data limit to zero, so set both explicitly (the compute-budget concept covers how). (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/media/content/upgrades/larger-transaction-sizes.mdx · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://docs.chainstack.com/docs/solana-transaction-v1.md, https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/docs/en/core/transactions/versioned-transactions.mdx, https://pond.dflow.net/spot/trading/v1-migration-guide
- [statement] A bot can cache a table's contents and re-fetch only to pick up new entries or to notice deactivation, meaning a deactivation_slot other than the maximum value in the table meta. Append-only entries and no re-creation at the same address mean a cached index never changes meaning. A cached copy that lacks a new entry cannot reference it, and a closed table makes the transaction fail. (medium confidence) — https://docs.anza.xyz/proposals/versioned-transactions · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://docs.rs/solana-address-lookup-table-interface/3.1.0/src/solana_address_lookup_table_interface/state.rs.html, https://github.com/solana-program/address-lookup-table/blob/main/program/src/processor.rs

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] 'Transaction simulation failed: This transaction has already been processed' on a resend means an identical message is already in the status cache. Read the signature's status instead of treating the send as failed. A Drift keeper bot logged that error and then failed with a 30-second 'not confirmed' timeout; a Drift maintainer attributed this class of error to congestion or an RPC node that fell behind. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/drift-labs/keeper-bots-v2/issues/130 · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://github.com/anza-xyz/agave/blob/v4.4.0/runtime/src/bank/check_transactions.rs
- [statement] Keypair files must stay out of git. Metaplex lists 'Never commit keypair files to git' and advises ignoring *.json. A CI secret scanner flags tracked files named id.json or *-keypair.json by filename alone, any JSON array of 64 integers 0-255, and base58 strings of about 86-90 characters. That scanner checks only the current tree, not history, so historical leaks need truffleHog or gitleaks, and exposed keys must be rotated rather than just deleted from git. (medium confidence) — https://metaplex.com/docs/solana/solana-keypairs-and-wallets · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://dev.to/sai_93caeceb4f6a4d9969910/a-free-github-action-that-fails-ci-on-leaked-solana-wallet-keys-how-i-built-and-shipped-3n9c
- [statement] A CU limit taken from a simulation can be too low at landing time, because account state changes between simulation and execution (swap routes through Token-2022 transfer hooks or changing tick arrays). The result is ComputationalBudgetExceeded and a paid, failed transaction. The sources suggest a 10-15% margin, re-simulating when a program is upgraded or the instruction mix changes, and caching typical CU use per transaction type instead of simulating every send. (medium confidence) — https://dev.to/verixia_233e4721792ce3390/optimizing-solana-compute-unit-limits-for-swap-execution-3di4 · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://orbitflare.com/blog/developers/solana-priority-fee-estimation, https://github.com/solana-labs/solana-web3.js/pull/2703
- [statement] Upgrading to web3.js v3 silently changes Connection's default commitment from finalized to confirmed. The code compiles unchanged, so the compiler cannot flag it; the official migration guide says 'omitted commitment now defaults to confirmed rather than finalized'. A bot that relied on finalized reads must pass the commitment explicitly on the Connection or per call, and should test against a real node because mocked tests keep passing with the old default. (high confidence) — https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-web3.js/blob/main/packages/web3.js/RELEASE_NOTES.md · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-web3.js/blob/main/docs/web3js-v1-to-v3-migration.md, https://www.quicknode.com/guides/solana-development/tooling/web3js/migrate-to-v3
- [statement] The table authority must sign every extend, freeze, deactivate and close. Entries are append-only, so an index always resolves to the same address (Anza made tables append-only to stop front-running). FreezeLookupTable sets the authority to None; after that the program refuses extend, deactivate and close ('Lookup table is frozen'), so the table's rent is locked for good. A bot that depends on someone else's table, such as a router's, must expect the authority to deactivate and close it, and should re-fetch table accounts before building instead of caching them indefinitely. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/solana-program/address-lookup-table/blob/main/program/src/processor.rs · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://docs.anza.xyz/proposals/versioned-transactions

## Facts and statements

- [statement] A blockhash is valid for about 150 blocks. The sources quote this window as roughly 1 minute 19 seconds, 60-90 seconds, or 80-90 seconds, depending on slot time. A transaction not processed in that window must be rebuilt with a new blockhash. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/cookbook/transactions/retry.mdx · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://www.helius.dev/blog/how-to-deal-with-blockhash-errors-on-solana, https://docs.chainstack.com/docs/solana-how-to-handle-the-transaction-expiry-error
- [statement] Re-sign with a new blockhash only after the current block height exceeds lastValidBlockHeight. Before then, the original transaction may still land, and a re-signed copy with a different blockhash is a distinct transaction that can also execute. The user then sees the same action twice. (high confidence) — https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/cookbook/transactions/retry.mdx · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://github.com/fardream/confirm-solana-transaction, https://docs.chainstack.com/docs/solana-how-to-handle-the-transaction-expiry-error
- [statement] Do not re-sign with a new blockhash until the original blockhash has expired. While it is still valid, both transactions can be accepted, and the user sees the same action twice. Re-sign only after the block height passes lastValidBlockHeight. (high confidence) — https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/cookbook/transactions/retry.mdx · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://docs.chainstack.com/docs/solana-how-to-handle-the-transaction-expiry-error, https://github.com/fardream/confirm-solana-transaction
- [statement] Do not treat a processed status as done. The retry guide documents a transaction that a leader on a minority fork processed and that was dropped before it finalized, and the Solana docs say processed data can change if the cluster switches forks. Under Alpenglow processed is unchanged and means only that a bank executed the transaction. (high confidence) — https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/cookbook/transactions/retry.mdx · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/docs/en/rpc/http/sendtransaction.mdx, https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/media/content/upgrades/alpenglow.mdx
- [statement] The Block Engine's bundle result protocol separates outcomes: Accepted (forwarded to a validator, possibly several), and Rejected with one of StateAuctionBidRejected (bid too low for its state auction), WinningBatchBidRejected (won its state auction but lost against other winners), SimulationFailure (names the offending tx signature), InternalError, or DroppedBundle. Block engines simulate bundles and pick the most profitable combinations. (medium confidence) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jito-labs/mev-protos/master/bundle.proto · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://docs.jito.wtf/lowlatencytxnsend/
- [statement] Put the tip instruction in the same transaction as the strategy logic, with post-transaction checks, so a failed strategy does not pay the tip. If space is tight, put state assertions (slot, balance) in the tip transaction. A standalone tip transaction inside a bundle increases exposure to 'uncle bandit' rebroadcast of individual bundle transactions. (medium confidence) — https://docs.jito.wtf/lowlatencytxnsend/ · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://rpcfast.com/blog/how-to-improve-your-jito-bundle-landing-rate-on-solana
- [statement] Atomicity does not hold if a block is uncled: bundle transactions can be rebroadcast individually outside the bundle ('unbundling'). Jito says Jito itself never leaks bundles, but during uncled-block situations users are exposed. Mitigation is pre/post account checks inside the transactions so a lone rebroadcast tx is harmless. (medium confidence) — https://docs.jito.wtf/lowlatencytxnsend/ · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://rpcfast.com/blog/how-to-improve-your-jito-bundle-landing-rate-on-solana
- [statement] Tips only influence a leader that runs Jito-Solana. Jito warns that tips do not prioritize transactions at validators that are not Jito-Solana leaders, so tipping then is wasted. Bundle inclusion is therefore tied to the slots where a Jito-enabled validator produces blocks. (high confidence) — https://docs.jito.wtf/lowlatencytxnsend/ · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://www.quicknode.com/builders-guide/tools/jito-bundles-by-jito-labs, https://rpcfast.com/blog/how-to-improve-your-jito-bundle-landing-rate-on-solana
- [statement] Jito publishes regional Block Engine URLs of the form https://<region>.mainnet.block-engine.jito.wtf (amsterdam, dublin, frankfurt, london, ny, slc, singapore, tokyo) plus a global geo-routed https://mainnet.block-engine.jito.wtf. Helius forwards bundles to the global endpoint and lets callers pick a region with the jito-region header (ams, dub, fra, lon, nyc, slc, sgp, tyo, mainnet). (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05) — https://docs.jito.wtf/lowlatencytxnsend/ · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://www.helius.dev/docs/sending-transactions/send-bundle
- [statement] Jito lists JSON-RPC SDKs for Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Rust and Go that wrap send_bundle, get_bundle_statuses, get_inflight_bundle_statuses, get_tip_accounts and send_transaction. Community code uses jito-ts for the gRPC SearcherClient. The third-party jito-bundle Rust crate adds tip strategies, pre-send checks (bundle size, lookup-table safety, transaction size) and confirmation polling across both the Jito API and Solana RPC. (medium confidence) — https://docs.jito.wtf/lowlatencytxnsend/ · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://docs.rs/crate/jito-bundle/0.1.4/source/FOR_USER.md, https://gist.github.com/zhe-t/60938c69e29276b7a9f098e1b0672c79
- [statement] Before Alpenglow activation Jito planned to put all mainnet BAM nodes into Maintenance Mode. Connected validators revert to the ordinary Jito-Agave Block Engine mode and keep accepting bundles through it, while the Maker Priority Plugin (MPP) and DBI are unavailable. DBI users are told to use the legacy Block Engine bundle path, and standard bundle senders have no action. BAM nodes return gradually after activation, with timing announced on Jito's Discord, so the post-activation state is not confirmed in the sources read. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-13) — https://solanacompass.com/news/jito-details-bams-alpenglow-plan-maintenance-mode-for-all-mainnet-nodes-no-firebam-during-the-transition · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://cryptobriefing.com/jito-bam-upgrade-cuts-bundle-delays/, https://solanacompass.com/news/jito-announces-bam-direct-bundle-ingest-routing-solana-bundles-past-the-block-engines-50ms-hop
- [statement] Put the tip instruction inside the same transaction as the strategy logic, with post-state assertions, so a failing strategy never pays the tip. If transaction space forces a separate tip transaction, add assertions to it (slot check, balance check) so the tip is conditional. Jito warns that standalone tip transactions inside bundles increase exposure to uncle-bandit scenarios. (high confidence) — https://docs.jito.wtf/lowlatencytxnsend/ · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://rpcfast.com/blog/how-to-improve-your-jito-bundle-landing-rate-on-solana
- [statement] jitodontfront: add any valid pubkey starting with jitodontfront as a read-only account to any instruction. The Block Engine then rejects any bundle containing that transaction unless it is at index 0. Several such transactions are allowed only if they are contiguous at the front and each shares a signer with the first. It works with sendTransaction, sendBundle and address lookup tables, runs on mainnet and testnet only, and the account need not exist on chain. Jito says it may reduce sandwich attacks but does not guarantee protection, and it applies only inside the Block Engine. (high confidence) — https://docs.jito.wtf/lowlatencytxnsend/ · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://solana.com/docs/defi/mev-protection, https://docs.chainstack.com/docs/solana-mev-protection
- [statement] DBI bundles do not appear in the Jito bundle explorer or its API, and DBI bundle IDs do not match Block Engine records. A JSON-RPC bundle ID means only that the node queued the request; a QUIC acknowledgment means only that the stream was accepted. Confirm landing with getSignatureStatuses on your own RPC using the transaction signatures. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-04) — https://bam.dev/docs/bam/dbi/ · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://github.com/jito-labs/bam-dbi, https://github.com/jito-labs/jito-docs/blob/main/docs/source/bundles.md
- [statement] Helius Sender (a Helius-run path across Helius, Jito, Harmonic and other routes) has stricter submission rules than the Jito Block Engine: a single transaction must carry both a tip transfer to a designated tip account and a compute-unit-price instruction or it is rejected, and sendBundle takes at most four transactions with at least one carrying the tip. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.helius.dev/docs/sending-transactions/sender · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots
- [statement] The Rust read_keypair parser expects the text to start with '[' and end with ']' (otherwise 'Input must be a JSON array'), splits on commas, requires exactly 64 u8 elements, and then runs the same pubkey check. write_keypair emits '[' plus 64 decimal values separated by commas with no spaces plus ']'. Other tools must produce this same shape for solana CLI and Rust programs to read the file. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.rs/crate/solana-keypair/latest/source/src/lib.rs · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://metaplex.com/docs/solana/solana-keypairs-and-wallets
- [statement] Keypair files are unencrypted. Matt Mazur notes the BIP39 passphrase protects the recovery seed phrase 'NOT the keypair file itself, which is stored as insecure plain text'. Metaplex's mitigation for a file-system wallet is chmod 600 on the file, and it recommends a hardware wallet or multisig for significant mainnet value. (medium confidence) — https://mattmazur.com/2021/11/19/splitting-a-solana-keypair-into-a-public-and-private-keys/ · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://metaplex.com/docs/solana/solana-keypairs-and-wallets
- [statement] Anza's remediation guidance after the web3.js compromise: verify that no application was ever built or deployed with 1.95.6 or 1.95.7 as a direct or transitive dependency, and rotate any suspect authority keys, explicitly including multisigs, program authorities and server keypairs. A bot whose keypair file or env var was loaded by an affected build should be treated as compromised. (high confidence) — https://www.anza.xyz/blog/web3-js-exploit-root-cause-analysis · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://helpnetsecurity.com/?p=318621
- [statement] Nothing encrypts a keypair file. The CLI itself warns that the BIP39 passphrase 'improves security of the recovery seed phrase NOT the keypair file itself, which is stored as insecure plain text' (quoted by Matt Mazur). Anza's file-system-wallet page says the file holds 'your unencrypted keypair', that the password 'applies to the recovery seed phrase, not the file', that file system wallets are 'the least secure method of storing SOL tokens', and that 'Anyone with access to this file will have access to all tokens sent to its public key'. (high confidence) — https://docs.anza.xyz/cli/wallets/file-system · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://mattmazur.com/2021/11/19/splitting-a-solana-keypair-into-a-public-and-private-keys/
- [statement] Rust Keypair deliberately has no Clone: the doc comment calls a second in-memory copy of secret keys 'usually a bad idea' and points to insecure_clone for tests or std::sync::Arc<Keypair> otherwise. TryFrom<&[u8]> copies the seed into a Zeroizing buffer so the transient copy is wiped. Signer is implemented for any Deref container (Box, Rc, Arc, &), so one Arc<Keypair> can be shared across bot tasks without copying key bytes. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.rs/crate/solana-keypair/latest/source/src/lib.rs · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://docs.rs/crate/solana-signer/latest/source/src/lib.rs
- [statement] Anza's guidance after the web3.js compromise: verify that no application was ever built and deployed with 1.95.6 or 1.95.7 as a direct or transitive dependency, and rotate any suspect authority keys, 'including but not limited to multisigs, program authorities, and server keypairs'. The advisory also asks developers to upgrade to 1.95.8, including those pinned to latest. A bot whose key file or env var was loaded by an affected build should be treated as exposed and rotated. (high confidence) — https://www.anza.xyz/blog/web3-js-exploit-root-cause-analysis · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jcxm-7wvp-g6p5
- [statement] OWASP and Docker both advise against passing secrets as environment variables. OWASP's Secrets Management Cheat Sheet lists mounted files, a secret-store fetch and environment variables as the three ways to inject a secret into a container, and says environment variables are 'generally accessible to all processes and may be included in logs or system dumps', so they are 'not recommended unless the other methods are not possible'. Docker Compose's secrets page says the same and mounts secrets as files at `/run/secrets/<secret_name>`, with per-service access and normal filesystem permissions. (high confidence) — https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Secrets_Management_Cheat_Sheet.html · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://docs.docker.com/compose/how-tos/use-secrets/
- [statement] The Solana Foundation's solana-keychain library (Rust, TypeScript, Python, Go) gives one signing interface over Memory, Vault, Privy, Turnkey, AWS KMS, Fireblocks, GCP KMS, Dfns, Para, CDP, Crossmint, Openfort, Utila and Fordefi backends, plus an opt-in, Rust-only Ledger backend. Its docs describe the Memory backend as 'Local keypairs, development, testing'. Kora, the Foundation's signer node, selects across a signer pool with `round_robin`, `random` or `weighted` strategies; its example config lists memory, Turnkey, Privy, Vault and Openfort signers, and its config code also defines AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Para, CDP and Dfns signer types. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-keychain · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-keychain/blob/main/python/README.md, https://github.com/solana-foundation/kora/blob/main/signers.example.toml, https://github.com/solana-foundation/kora/blob/main/crates/lib/src/signer/config.rs
- [statement] The fee market is per writable account, so estimates should pass the writable state accounts the transaction will lock (pool, token accounts, oracle). Passing a program ID returns near-empty data and a misleading picture; omitting accounts gives a network-wide view that is wrong for contested accounts. (medium confidence) — https://docs.chainstack.com/docs/solana-estimate-priority-fees-getrecentprioritizationfees · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://orbitflare.com/blog/developers/solana-priority-fee-estimation, https://www.helius.dev/docs/rpc/guides/getrecentprioritizationfees
- [statement] Estimate the price per account set, not network-wide. Pass the writable accounts the transaction will lock (pool state, vaults, user token accounts) to getRecentPrioritizationFees. Do not pass program IDs: programs are read-only in user transactions, so the per-account fee map holds almost no data for them and the result misleads. (high confidence) — https://docs.chainstack.com/docs/solana-estimate-priority-fees-getrecentprioritizationfees · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://orbitflare.com/blog/developers/solana-priority-fee-estimation, https://www.helius.dev/docs/rpc/guides/getrecentprioritizationfees
- [statement] A durable-nonce transaction must carry System AdvanceNonceAccount as instruction 0 (NONCED_TX_MARKER_IX_INDEX = 0, with the nonce account first and writable). Otherwise the runtime does not treat it as a nonce transaction, so the nonce value used as recent_blockhash is not accepted. Add Compute Budget instructions after instruction 0. Solana's Kit example sets the nonce lifetime first, which prepends AdvanceNonceAccount, and adds the other instructions afterwards. (high confidence) — https://github.com/anza-xyz/solana-sdk/blob/master/svm-transaction/src/svm_message.rs · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/docs/en/core/transactions/durable-nonces.mdx
- [statement] The default simulation commitment is finalized. Helius says a blockhash fetched at confirmed can look too new to an RPC that validates against finalized, so simulateTransaction should be called with replaceRecentBlockhash set, and preflightCommitment should match the commitment used to fetch the blockhash. (medium confidence) — https://www.helius.dev/blog/how-to-deal-with-blockhash-errors-on-solana · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://github.com/solana-foundation/developer-content/blob/e3ab72171725e4089be130f4a481288533e59f0a/docs/rpc/http/simulateTransaction.mdx
- [statement] Triton's `/sendtx` endpoint always submits without a preflight simulation and does not support `skipPreflight: false`, so a bot that sends through it must run `simulateTransaction` through the normal RPC interface first. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.triton.one/solana/faq/sending-transactions.md · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://docs.triton.one/solana/sending-transactions/best-practices.md
- [statement] A reconstructed bot case from a vendor-adjacent post says failures first read as 'slippage exceeded' were stale state: the shared RPC ran 2-3 slots behind and the simulation at submit time used stale data. The post calls itself a composite case, so use it only as illustration. (low confidence) — https://www.troopmessenger.com/blogs/solana-mev-bot-wrong-infrastructure · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots
- [statement] Simulating from a fee payer that holds no SOL returns 'Attempt to debit an account but found no record of a prior credit.'; Metaplex says this means the account has no SOL. (low confidence) — https://metaplex.com/docs/guides/general/how-to-diagnose-solana-transaction-errors · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots
- [statement] A bot can read the effect of a transaction without landing it. The accounts config returns post-simulation account data for chosen addresses, and the result includes preBalances, postBalances, preTokenBalances and postTokenBalances, from which a net lamport or token change can be computed. These values describe only the simulation bank's state at the chosen commitment. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/1587255d379037f4af77843e0231cec006cdb1c5/apps/docs/content/docs/en/rpc/http/simulatetransaction.mdx · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://github.com/anza-xyz/agave/blob/v3.1.8/rpc/src/rpc.rs
- [statement] In Python, solders (Rust bindings) supplies the core types (Keypair, Pubkey, Instruction, MessageV0, VersionedTransaction), RPC request and response types, and a LiteSVM test VM (solders.litesvm) that Solana's docs call a much faster alternative to solana-test-validator. solders does no networking. solana-py is built on solders and supplies AsyncClient, SolanaWsClient and SPL Token helpers. Solana's docs list both under community clients and recommend solana-py for networking and async RPC. (high confidence) — https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/docs/en/clients/community/python.mdx · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://github.com/michaelhly/solana-py, https://kevinheavey.github.io/solders/tutorials/transactions.html, https://github.com/kevinheavey/solders/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
- [statement] Transaction signers may not be loaded through a lookup table; signer addresses must be serialized in full in the message. (low confidence) — https://docs.anza.xyz/proposals/versioned-transactions · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots
- [statement] A tutorial says creating a table costs about 0.003 SOL rent and each extendLookupTable instruction can add about 30 addresses (limited by transaction size), so filling a 256-entry table takes several transactions. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.chainstack.com/docs/solana-address-lookup-tables.md · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots
- [statement] Addresses appended to a lookup table are unusable in the slot they were added. The table records last_extended_slot and last_extended_slot_start_index; while the current slot is not past last_extended_slot, only entries below that start index resolve, so older entries keep working. A bot that extends a table and builds, simulates or sends a transaction with the new entries in the same slot gets a failed lookup (an out-of-range index, reported as InvalidAddressLookupTableIndex). Wait for the next slot. Each extend must also leave the table rent-exempt, so the payer funds the added rent. (high confidence) — https://docs.rs/solana-address-lookup-table-interface/3.1.0/src/solana_address_lookup_table_interface/state.rs.html · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://github.com/solana-program/address-lookup-table/blob/main/program/src/processor.rs, https://docs.anza.xyz/proposals/versioned-transactions, https://docs.chainstack.com/docs/solana-address-lookup-tables.md, https://github.com/anza-xyz/solana-sdk/blob/master/transaction-error/src/lib.rs
- [statement] Jupiter Swap V2 GET /swap/v2/build returns addressesByLookupTableAddress, an object that maps each lookup table address to its account array, so no separate RPC fetch of table accounts is needed. /build returns instruction objects, and the integrator assembles, simulates, signs and sends the transaction (v0 by default). maxAccounts takes 1 to 64 and defaults to 64. In Jupiter's docs, 'V1' in the migration table means Jupiter's old API version, not Solana Transaction V1. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://developers.jup.ag/docs/swap/v2/migration.md · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://developers.jup.ag/docs/swap/advanced/reduce-transaction-size.md, https://developers.jup.ag/docs/swap/advanced/transaction-versions.md
- [statement] Tables are append-only. ExtendLookupTable adds entries and nothing removes or reorders them. The program rejects an empty extension, a full table, and an extension that would pass 256 entries, and only the table authority can extend. Entries are never rewritten, so an index that resolved to an address once resolves to it for the table's lifetime. (high confidence) — https://github.com/solana-program/address-lookup-table/blob/main/program/src/processor.rs · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://docs.anza.xyz/proposals/versioned-transactions, https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/docs/en/core/transactions/versioned-transactions.mdx
- [statement] Do not send value-moving transactions that depend on a table that is not yet finalized. The Anza proposal warns that an attacker could fork the chain just after a table is created and add a different entry in the fork. It advises waiting for the table to be finalized and optionally adding integrity-check instructions. Tutorials and the Solana docs example wait only one slot after an extend. (medium confidence) — https://docs.anza.xyz/proposals/versioned-transactions · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/docs/en/core/transactions/versioned-transactions.mdx, https://docs.chainstack.com/docs/solana-address-lookup-tables.md
- [statement] Jupiter's current Swap V2 /build endpoint returns addressesByLookupTableAddress: the tables to compile against on v0, and an empty object on v1. The Metis Swap API page now carries a banner saying that API is no longer actively maintained and is superseded by Swap V2. Code copied from the older swap-instructions examples may therefore sit on a legacy path. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://developers.jup.ag/docs/swap/advanced/transaction-versions · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://developers.jup.ag/docs/swap/requote-with-lower-max-accounts
- [statement] A v1 transaction starts with version byte 0x81 at offset 0 and carries its signatures at the tail with no length prefix. Counts are fixed-width u8 fields, and instruction headers come before the payloads. Legacy and v0 start with a compact-u16 signature count; v0's 0x80 is the first byte of the message, after the signatures. A parser that expects a leading signature array fails on v1 bytes. (high confidence) — https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/docs/en/core/transactions/versioned-transactions.mdx · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-improvement-documents/blob/main/proposals/0385-transaction-v1.md, https://docs.chainstack.com/docs/solana-transaction-v1.md, https://www.helius.dev/docs/rpc/transaction-v1.md
